newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers clash with soldiers in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers clash with soldiers in Hebron.

text.p: Jewish settlers hurled eggs and flower pots at Israeli troops but couldn't keep them from heightening a gate separating Jews and Arabs in Hebron's volatile Old City, witnesses said.
"We will not live in ghettos," shouted one of the 50 settlers who also turned water hoses on the security forces.
Soldiers pushed and dragged settlers away. Police detained one settler who had a knife in his hand.
Police and soldiers added barbed wire to the gate separating the Beit Hadassah Jewish enclave from Palestinian houses and shops in the heart of the West Bank city still under Israeli occupation.

The city has long been a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence, most recently in clashes which erupted over the start of construction of a Jewish settlement last month on Jerusalem land claimed by both sides.
The gate was erected in 1994 to reduce friction after a Jewish settler Baruch Goldstein massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in a Hebron mosque before being beaten to death by survivors.
